title: Composition coherence for adjoint restriction-kernel diagrams
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal E$ be small sites with abelian sheaf categories [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $v:\mathcal D\to\mathcal E$ be functors whose precomposition preserves abelian sheaves. Write $R(G)(W)=G(uW)$ and $R_v(H)(W)=H(vW)$ for these precomposition functors. Suppose $L\dashv R$ and $M\dashv R_v$ are additive adjunctions with exact left adjoints. Let $m:V\to T$, $m':V'\to T'$, and $m'':V''\to T''$ be monomorphisms in the three sites. Let $t:T'\to uT$, $s:V'\to uV$, $t':T''\to vT'$, and $s':V''\to vV'$ satisfy $u(m)s=tm'$ and $v(m')s'=t'm''$. For cochain complexes $I,J,P$ on $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal E$ respectively, let $h:LI\to J$ and $k:MJ\to P$ be chain maps. Define the restriction-kernel diagram $D_m(I)=[\ker(I(T)\to I(V))\to I(T)\to I(V)]$ and its adjoint diagram maps as in [lem-pur-support-pair-chain-coherence](1). Then the diagram map for $k\circ M(h)$ and the composite data $(v\circ u,v(t)\circ t',v(s)\circ s')$ equals the composite of the diagram maps for $h$ and $k$, under the unit-compatible identification of the composite adjunction with $(M\circ L)\dashv(R\circ R_v)$. The same identity holds on cohomology for derived coefficient morphisms represented on bounded-below injective complexes, independently of representative choices as in [lem-pur-support-pair-chain-coherence](2).

proof.text: Take the degreewise adjoints $b:I\to RJ$ of $h$ and $c:J\to R_vP$ of $k$. The composite data satisfy the hypotheses of [lem-pur-support-pair-chain-coherence] for $v\circ u$: precomposition with $v\circ u$ is $R\circ R_v$, which preserves abelian sheaves; $M\circ L$ is additive and exact and left adjoint to $R\circ R_v$ through the composite Hom bijection; and $(vu)(m)\circ v(s)s'=v(u(m)s)s'=v(tm')s'=v(t)\,v(m')s'=v(t)t'm''$. Under that Hom bijection the adjoint of $k\circ M(h)$ is $R(c)\circ b$, since transposing $k\circ M(h)$ across $M\dashv R_v$ gives $R_v$-adjoint $c\circ h$, whose transpose across $L\dashv R$ is $R(c)\circ b$. Apply clause (1) of [lem-pur-support-pair-chain-coherence] to $h$, to $k$, and to $k\circ M(h)$ with the composite data. The T-component for the composite is $P(v(t)t')\circ c_{uT}\circ b_T=P(t')\circ P(v(t))\circ c_{uT}\circ b_T$. Naturality of the sheaf map $c:J\to R_vP$ along $t:T'\to uT$ gives $P(v(t))\circ c_{uT}=c_{T'}\circ J(t)$, so this equals $(P(t')\circ c_{T'})\circ(J(t)\circ b_T)$, the composite of the T-components for $k$ and for $h$. The same computation with $s,s'$ and naturality of $c$ along $s$ gives the V-components. The kernel inclusions are monomorphisms, so the kernel map of the composite, being the unique map compatible with the inclusions, equals the composite of the two kernel maps. Hence the diagram map for $k\circ M(h)$ and $(v\circ u,v(t)\circ t',v(s)\circ s')$ is the composite of the diagram maps for $h$ and $k$.

proof.text: If h is replaced by a homotopic representative, clause (2) of [lem-pur-support-pair-chain-coherence] supplies compatible homotopies on the T-, V-, and kernel components; applying the degreewise adjoint of the homotopy for h and then the chain map k gives the same homotopy for the composite. The analogous assertion holds when k is changed. Thus the chain-level equality in Step 1 survives passage to cohomology, and the two routes induce the same maps on all three cohomology groups.

source.place: Section 9, Theorem 9.4, pp. 65-67, functoriality and independence of injective representatives; Stacks derived.tex Tag 070I

proof.text: For bounded-below injective representatives $I,J,P$, clause (2) of [lem-pur-support-pair-chain-coherence] says that every derived morphism has a chain representative unique up to homotopy and that the three induced cohomology maps are unchanged under replacing representatives. Since $M$ is exact, $Q(M(h))$ is $M$ applied to the derived morphism represented by $h$, so $k\circ M(h)$ represents the composite derived morphism. Apply clause (2) once to $h$, once to $k$, and once to the composite with the data checked in Step 1. The equality from Steps 1–2 is therefore independent of all representative choices and is precisely the asserted composition identity on cohomology.
